name: Cardinals
facts: It is the oldest continuously operating professional football club in the United States, tracing back to an 1898 neighborhood athletic club.
Secondhand maroon jerseys bought from the University of Chicago in 1901 had faded so far that the owner renamed the club for the shade of red he saw instead.
It has represented Chicago, St. Louis and the desert Southwest over its history.
It won NFL championships in 1925 and 1947, both while based in Chicago.
A safety left the roster to enlist in the Army Rangers after 9/11 and was killed in Afghanistan; a statue of him stands at the stadium.
It reached its first Super Bowl after the 2008 season and lost 27-23 on a touchdown inside the final minute.
Home games are played under a retractable roof, on a natural grass field that rolls out of the building on a tray.
A receiver spent all 17 of his NFL seasons here and retired second on the all-time receiving yards list.

name: Falcons
facts: The very first draft pick in its history was the No. 1 overall selection of the 1966 draft, a linebacker.
A two-sport star played here in the late 1980s and once hit a major league home run and scored an NFL touchdown in the same week.
It went 14-2 in 1998 behind a running back who gained more than 1,800 yards on the ground.
A quarterback here became the first at his position to rush for 1,000 yards in a season, in 2006.
A receiver here gained 300 yards in a single game in 2016.
Its quarterback won MVP in 2016 with a 117.1 passer rating.
It led a Super Bowl 28-3 in the third quarter and lost.
Home games are played under a retractable roof that opens in eight triangular petals like a camera lens.

name: Ravens
facts: The nickname was picked in a fan phone-in poll and honors a poem written by a one-time resident of the city.
Its first draft pick was an offensive tackle who made 11 Pro Bowls and reached the Hall of Fame.
The franchise arrived in 1996 when an owner moved his team from another city, leaving the old name and record book behind.
Its 2000 defense gave up 165 points, the fewest of any 16-game season, and pitched four shutouts.
A middle linebacker played all 17 of his seasons for the franchise and retired minutes after winning a title.
It won a Super Bowl in a game interrupted by a 34-minute stadium power outage.
A quarterback drafted here in 2018 won a unanimous MVP the next year after setting the single-season rushing record for his position.

name: Bills
facts: It won back-to-back AFL championships in 1964 and 1965, before the leagues merged.
A running back here became the first to rush for 2,000 yards in a season, and did it in only 14 games.
Its early-1990s offense ran a no-huddle scheme known as the K-Gun.
It won a playoff game after trailing 35-3, the largest comeback in NFL postseason history.
Lake-effect snow has twice forced its home games to be relocated to a domed stadium in another state.
A missed 47-yard field goal in the final seconds cost it the Super Bowl after the 1990 season.
It lost four Super Bowls in a row, after the 1990 through 1993 seasons.
Its fan base is famous for breaking folding tables at tailgates and for donating en masse to charities tied to opposing players.

name: Panthers
facts: It played its entire inaugural season in a college stadium in a neighboring state while its own was finished.
It won a division title and reached a conference championship game in only its second season.
Its rallying slogan comes from a speech a terminally ill linebacker gave the team in 2003.
Its logo shape is said to trace the combined outline of the two states in its name.
It lost a Super Bowl 32-29 on a field goal with four seconds left.
A 5-foot-9 receiver retired as its all-time leader in catches, yards and touchdowns.
It went 15-1 in 2015 and its quarterback was the league MVP.

name: Bears
facts: It entered the league in 1920 as a company team for a starch manufacturer in Decatur, Illinois.
Its 1940 championship game win was 73-0, the most lopsided result of the NFL's first century.
A rookie here scored six touchdowns in a single game in 1965.
By 2025 it had sent more players to the Pro Football Hall of Fame than any other franchise.
It is one of only two franchises that have been in the NFL continuously since 1920.
Its 1985 defense ran a scheme named after a jersey number and allowed 10 points total in three playoff games.
A running back retired in 1987 as the league's all-time leading rusher with 16,726 yards.
Since 1971 home games have been played on a city lakefront, in a stadium that opened in 1924 as a war memorial.

name: Bengals
facts: It was founded in 1968 by a coach who had built another Ohio franchise and then been fired from it.
Its striped helmet arrived in 1981, replacing a plain orange shell that had carried only block letters.
A touchdown celebration called the Ickey Shuffle came out of its 1988 Super Bowl team.
It lost two Super Bowls in the 1980s to the same opponent, both by fewer than six points.
It went 31 seasons without a playoff win, from the 1990 season to the 2021 season.
A receiver here legally changed his surname in 2008 to a Spanish play on his jersey number, 85.
It reached the Super Bowl after the 2021 season behind a quarterback taken first overall a year earlier.

name: Browns
facts: It won all four championships of the league it began in, then joined the NFL in 1950.
It won the NFL title in its very first NFL season.
Its helmet has never carried a logo.
A fullback here won eight rushing titles in nine seasons and walked away at the peak of his career.
The franchise was shut down for three seasons in the late 1990s while its name and records stayed behind in the city.
A left tackle here played 10,363 consecutive snaps.
It finished 0-16 in 2017.
A cornerback nicknamed the 1985 defense after dogs, and the bleachers behind one end zone took the name; the fans in them bark and wear dog masks.

name: Cowboys
facts: It went 0-11-1 in its first season.
Its nickname as the country's team came from the narration of a 1978 season highlight film.
A hole in its old stadium's roof was said to exist so that God could watch His favorite team play.
Its defense in the early 1970s was known as the Doomsday Defense.
It played in five Super Bowls in the 1970s and won two of them.
A running back here retired as the NFL's all-time leading rusher with 18,355 yards.
It won three Super Bowls in four seasons in the 1990s.
Its current stadium hangs a video board so low over the field that a punt once struck it.

name: Broncos
facts: Its first uniforms included vertically striped socks so unpopular that a new coach had them burned at a public bonfire in 1962.
Its 1977 defense was nicknamed the Orange Crush.
A 98-yard march in the 1986 conference championship game is remembered simply as The Drive.
It lost its first four Super Bowls, three of them by 19 points or more.
A running back here gained 2,008 yards on the ground in 1998.
Its quarterback won back-to-back Super Bowls and retired immediately after the second.
Its 2013 offense scored 606 points, the most any team had managed in a season at the time.
It won a Super Bowl after the 2015 season with a defense that led the league in yards allowed and a quarterback playing his last game.

name: Lions
facts: The franchise began in Portsmouth, Ohio, and moved to its current city in 1934.
It has hosted a game on Thanksgiving Day in nearly every season since 1934.
It won NFL championships in 1935, 1952, 1953 and 1957.
A running back abruptly retired in 1999 while still within 1,500 yards of the all-time rushing record.
A receiver here gained 1,964 yards in 2012, the most in a season by anyone at the time.
It finished 0-16 in 2008, the first team ever to do so.
It won its first playoff game in 32 years after the 2023 season.
Its fans rally around a two-word chant built on the collective noun for a group of its namesake animal.

name: Packers
facts: It is named for the meat-packing company that paid for its first jerseys in 1919.
It is the only community-owned, non-profit franchise in the NFL, with hundreds of thousands of shareholders.
It won three consecutive league championships twice, in 1929-31 and again in 1965-67.
The 1967 championship game it hosted, played at 13 below zero, is known as the Ice Bowl.
The Super Bowl trophy is named after its head coach of the 1960s.
It won nine league championships before the Super Bowl existed, more than any other franchise.
Two of its quarterbacks won a combined seven MVP awards in back-to-back eras.
Its signature touchdown celebration is a jump into the arms of fans in the front row.

name: Texans
facts: It was awarded to a city that had just lost its previous franchise to another state.
It won its very first game as an expansion team, beating an in-state rival in 2002.
It did not make the playoffs until its tenth season of existence.
Its logo is a bull's head whose contours form the outline of a state.
Its mascot is a bull named Toro.
A defensive end here won three Defensive Player of the Year awards in four seasons.
It plays in the first NFL stadium ever built with a retractable roof.

name: Colts
facts: Its quarterback of the 1950s had been cut by another team and was playing semi-pro football when it signed him for about $7,000.
The franchise left its old city overnight in March 1984, loading everything into moving vans during a snowstorm.
The overtime championship game it won in 1958 is called the Greatest Game Ever Played.
It lost Super Bowl III to an AFL team whose quarterback had publicly guaranteed victory.
It won its first Super Bowl on a field goal with five seconds left despite committing seven turnovers.
A quarterback here won four MVP awards in a single decade with the franchise.
It started 0-13 in 2011 and then took a quarterback first overall.
Its stadium has a retractable roof and a huge window that frames the downtown skyline.

name: Jaguars
facts: Its first head coach had coached receivers on a Super Bowl-winning staff and took it to four playoff berths in five years.
It reached a conference championship game in only its second season as an expansion team.
It drafted first overall in consecutive years, 2021 and 2022.
It has played at least one home game in London in nearly every season since 2013.
It won a playoff game after the 2017 season behind a defense that allowed fewer passing yards than any other.
It erased a 27-0 deficit to win a playoff game 31-30 after the 2022 season.
Its stadium has two swimming pools built into one end zone and some of the largest video boards in the league.

name: Chiefs
facts: It began in 1960 in Dallas under a different name and moved in 1963.
Its founder also founded the entire league it started out in.
Its founder coined the phrase 'Super Bowl' after watching his children play with a bouncy toy ball.
A linebacker here set the single-game sack record with seven in 1990.
A tight end it drafted in 1997 retired as the most productive player ever at his position.
It won the fourth Super Bowl ever played and then waited 50 years to win another.
Its stadium set a Guinness world record in 2014 with a 142.2-decibel crowd roar.
It won three Super Bowls in five seasons, after the 2019, 2022 and 2023 seasons.

name: Chargers
facts: It played its first season in one city, spent 56 years in another, then moved back in 2017.
It won the 1963 AFL championship 51-10.
Its high-volume passing offense of the late 1970s was nicknamed Air Coryell.
A brutally humid 1981 playoff win in Miami is remembered as the Epic in Miami.
A linebacker it drafted in 1990 made 12 straight Pro Bowls.
A running back here scored 28 rushing touchdowns in 2006 and won MVP.
Powder blue uniforms from its 1960s past became its primary look again in 2020.
It shares a stadium with another NFL team in the same city.

name: Rams
facts: It was the first NFL team to paint a logo on its helmets, done by hand in 1948.
It is the only franchise to win league championships representing three different cities.
Its defensive line of the 1960s was known as the Fearsome Foursome.
A running back here set the single-season rushing record with 2,105 yards in 1984.
Its 1999 offense was nicknamed the Greatest Show on Turf and won a Super Bowl on a tackle made a yard short of the goal line.
It returned to its current city in 2016 after 21 seasons in Missouri.
A defensive tackle here won three Defensive Player of the Year awards in a four-year span.
It won a Super Bowl played in its own stadium after the 2021 season.

name: Raiders
facts: Its original center started every game of the franchise's first 15 seasons.
A 1978 play in which the ball was deliberately batted forward into the end zone forced the league to rewrite a rule.
Its owner sued the NFL over relocation rights and won, which set up two different moves.
It has had four different home-city stints across three cities.
It lost a 1972 playoff game on a deflected last-second touchdown that got its own nickname.
Its motto, from its longtime owner, is 'Just Win, Baby'.
A running back won Super Bowl MVP here with a 74-yard touchdown run after the 1983 season.
It moved to the desert in 2020 into a black domed stadium that cost about $1.9 billion.

name: Dolphins
facts: Its head coach arrived in 1970 from a Baltimore team and stayed 26 seasons.
Its early-1970s defense was called the No-Name Defense.
A quarterback here faked a spike and threw a touchdown instead in 1994.
It won consecutive Super Bowls after the 1972 and 1973 seasons.
Its 1972 team went 17-0, the only perfect season, playoffs included, of the NFL's first century.
A quarterback here threw for 5,084 yards and 48 touchdowns in 1984.
Its coach retired as the winningest in NFL history with 347 victories.
Home games are played under a canopy that shades the seats but leaves the field open.

name: Vikings
facts: A defensive tackle here won MVP in 1971, the first defensive player ever to do it.
Its defensive line of the 1970s was nicknamed the Purple People Eaters.
It lost four Super Bowls between the 1969 and 1976 seasons.
It lost a home conference championship game after a 15-1 season on a missed field goal by a kicker who had not missed all year.
A running back here gained 296 yards on the ground in a single 2007 game.
A running back here returned from a torn knee ligament to rush for 2,097 yards and win MVP.
It won a playoff game after the 2017 season on a 61-yard touchdown with no time left.
Its crowd performs a slow-building synchronized clap borrowed from Icelandic soccer fans.

name: Patriots
facts: Its name was chosen by a fan contest in 1960, and it played in four different stadiums in its first decade.
It lost its first two Super Bowl appearances by 36 and by 14 points.
A sixth-round pick from 2000 took over as its starter in 2001 after the incumbent was injured.
A 2001 playoff win in a snowstorm turned on an obscure rule about a quarterback's arm motion.
It went 16-0 in the 2007 regular season and then lost the Super Bowl.
It erased a 28-3 deficit to win a Super Bowl in overtime.
It won six Super Bowls in an 18-season stretch with the same coach and quarterback.
It won three titles in five years, after the 2014, 2016 and 2018 seasons.

name: Saints
facts: The franchise was awarded on a Catholic feast day in 1966, and took its nickname straight from it.
A kicker here made a 63-yard field goal in 1970 that went unmatched for 28 years and unbeaten for 43.
Fans wore paper bags over their heads through a 1-15 season in 1980.
It did not win a playoff game until its 34th season.
Its stadium sheltered thousands of evacuees after a 2005 hurricane, and the team played that entire season away from home.
It won its Super Bowl partly on a surprise onside kick to open the second half.
A quarterback here threw for 5,000 yards in five different seasons.
A missed pass interference call in a conference championship game got the rule made reviewable.

name: Giants
facts: The franchise was bought for $500 in 1925 and stayed in the same family for close to a century.
It won a 1934 championship game by switching to sneakers on a frozen field at halftime.
It won NFL championships in 1927, 1934, 1938 and 1956.
A linebacker taken second overall in 1981 won league MVP as a defensive player in 1986.
A defensive end here set the single-season sack record with 22.5 in 2001.
It beat an undefeated team in the Super Bowl after the 2007 season, helped by a catch pinned against a helmet.
It beat the same opponent in two Super Bowls four years apart, an underdog both times.
It shares a New Jersey stadium with another franchise.

name: Jets
facts: It started in 1960 under an entirely different name and changed it in 1963 when new owners took over.
Its defensive line around 1981 earned a nickname riffing on the city's stock exchange.
A running back here won the 2004 rushing title at 31, by a single yard.
A cornerback here was so hard to throw at that his coverage area got its own island nickname.
Its quarterback publicly guaranteed a Super Bowl win and then delivered a 16-7 upset.
That win, after the 1968 season, was the first by an AFL team over an NFL champion.
It reached back-to-back conference championship games after the 2009 and 2010 seasons.
It shares a New Jersey stadium with another franchise.

name: Eagles
facts: It merged with an in-state rival for a single wartime season in 1943 and fielded one combined team.
A center-linebacker here played both ways full time in 1960, the last NFL player to do so.
Its old stadium had a working courtroom and holding cell in the basement for unruly fans.
It won NFL championships in 1948, 1949 and 1960.
Its fans are still reminded that they once booed and threw snowballs at a Santa Claus.
It won a Super Bowl with a backup quarterback who also caught a touchdown pass on a trick play.
Its short-yardage quarterback push became so unstoppable that the league debated outlawing it.
It won its second Super Bowl after the 2024 season by 18 points.

name: Steelers
facts: It was originally named after the city's baseball club.
Its helmet logo appears on only one side, a holdover from a 1962 experiment that was never undone.
Its colors are taken from the city's flag.
Its 1970s defensive front was named in a 1971 radio contest that welded the city industry onto a Cold War phrase.
It won a 1972 playoff game on a deflected pass scooped up inches off the turf and run in for a score.
It won four Super Bowls in six seasons in the 1970s.
It won its sixth Super Bowl after the 2008 season on a toe-tap catch in the corner of the end zone.
Its fans wave gold towels that have raised millions for a local school for people with disabilities.

name: Seahawks
facts: As part of its expansion deal it played its first season in one conference and its second in the other.
It is the only franchise to have appeared in a championship game in both conferences.
Its jersey number 12 is retired in honor of its fans.
A 67-yard playoff touchdown run after the 2010 season was so violent that it registered on a nearby seismometer.
Its stadium was deliberately designed to trap and amplify crowd noise, and its fans have twice set the world record for loudest crowd.
Its hard-hitting 2013 secondary earned a nickname of its own and won a Super Bowl 43-8 over the highest-scoring offense in NFL history to that point.
It lost the following Super Bowl on an interception at the one-yard line.
It won a second Super Bowl after the 2025 season, beating a six-time champion 29-13.

name: 49ers
facts: It is named for the prospectors of an 1849 gold rush.
It was one of three teams taken into the NFL for 1950 when a rival league folded.
Its 1950s backfield was called the Million Dollar Backfield, and all four members reached the Hall of Fame.
A late touchdown pass in the 1981 conference championship game is remembered simply as The Catch.
Its system of timed, short, rhythmic passes became known as the West Coast offense.
A receiver here retired with 197 receiving touchdowns and 22,895 receiving yards.
It won five Super Bowls between the 1981 and 1994 seasons.
Since 2014 it has played about 40 miles from the city in its name.

name: Buccaneers
facts: It lost the first 26 games in its history.
Its original orange uniforms and winking pirate logo earned the era the nickname Creamsicle.
It reached a conference championship game in only its fourth season.
It had 14 consecutive losing seasons from 1983 through 1996.
Its 2002 defense allowed the fewest points in the league and won a Super Bowl 48-21.
Its home end zone holds a 103-foot pirate ship whose cannons fire after scores.
It signed a 42-year-old quarterback in March 2020 and won the title with him that season, by which time he had turned 43.
It was the first team ever to win a Super Bowl played in its own stadium.

name: Titans
facts: It won the first two championships of the league it helped found, in 1960 and 1961.
Its late-1970s teams had a rallying cry and fight song called Luv Ya Blue.
It spent two seasons under a transitional name, playing in two different cities in the same state before settling in 1999.
A running back here won MVP in 1979 and then rushed for 1,934 yards in 1980.
It lost a playoff game in which it had led 35-3.
It won a playoff game on a kickoff return with a lateral, now known as the Music City Miracle.
It lost a Super Bowl when a receiver was tackled one yard short of the end zone on the final play.
A running back here rushed for 2,027 yards in 2020.

name: Commanders
facts: It began in Boston in 1932 and won a championship in its very first season after relocating in 1937.
Its quarterback in 1943 led the league in passing, punting and interceptions in the same season.
Its offensive line of the 1980s was nicknamed the Hogs.
A cornerback here played all 20 of his NFL seasons for the franchise.
It won a Super Bowl with the first Black starting quarterback to do so, who threw four touchdown passes in one quarter.
It won three Super Bowls in a decade with three different starting quarterbacks.
It won NFL championships in 1937 and 1942, before the Super Bowl existed.
It changed its team name twice in three years, in 2020 and again in 2022.
